subject: Pelican POC: request for onboarding warmup residency & cache-seeding
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pelican POC: request for onboarding warmup residency & cache-seeding

Team —

Quick context: Pelican Health (enterprise prospect, PEL-4921) is moving to a short POC week (Apr 5–12) and has a firm latency requirement: 85th percentile < 80ms for their clinical assistant flows. During our perf run last week they saw a large cold-start tail when their traffic first hits the model; they asked if we can temporarily guarantee lower tail latency during onboarding.

They've proposed two things they'd like us to support for the POC:
- Temporary model residency reserved for the account for the first 72 hours of the POC (so their model instance stays warm)
- Cache-seeding/prefix pre-warm for their top ~10 prefixes (we can provide the list) so KV lookups/attention warm path is primed

Why this matters: Pelican will run live clinical traffic during POC and their procurement/legal team will only sign if we can demonstrably meet the SLO during ramp. This ask is narrowly scoped to the POC window — they expect the warmup to be reversible and auditable.

Attachments: pelican_poc_latency_snapshot.pdf (sample trace), pelican_top_prefixes.csv

Ask: can Eng/Product scope & estimate a minimal-safe implementation that supports a 72h onboarding warmup mode (pin + cache-seed) and whether we can commit to a timeline to have it ready before Apr 4 (Pelican wants warmup started Apr 4). If not doable, what's the closest mitigation we can offer (prefill via synthetic traffic, guided role for their engineers to run a seeding harness, etc.)

Pls advise earliest — will set up a short design sync once we have rough estimates.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pelican POC: request for onboarding warmup residency & cache-seeding

Thanks Jasmine — a few clarifying q's before I size: 

1) Residency: do they need a full dedicated GPU slot (exclusive) or would a soft pin (preferential routing to a small dedicated pool) be acceptable? Exclusive residency has stronger latency guarantees but is heavier on capacity.

2) Cache-seed: are the "top 10 prefixes" short prompts we can replay into the prefix/KV cache, or are they live user histories that contain PHI — that affects how we handle stores/replay for compliance. If it's PHI, we need a secure replay path or customer-supplied seeding harness.

3) Model/quantization: which model and quant profile are they requesting? Warmup looks different for FP16 vs 4-bit quantized weights.

Possible approaches I see:
- Short-term exclusive residency: pin model instance on 1 GPU for 72h; orchestrator marks the slot reserved and rejects other tenants; plus a background seeding job that replays prefixes (synthetic/scrubbed) to populate KV cache.
- Soft-residency + aggressive pre-warm: route requests to a small reserved pool and run a synthetic warmup runner that hits the same prefixes at ramp start. More capacity-efficient but higher chance of tail.

High-level estimate: 2–3 eng-weeks to add a config flag + orchestrator gating + controlled seeding job, assuming no extra security gating. If we need a compliant replay pipeline for PHI, add 1–2 weeks and involve Security.

I can dig into an implementation sketch and list of needed changes if product wants to proceed.

-Dev
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pelicanhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: eng-ops@pelicanhealth.com
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Pelican POC: request for onboarding warmup residency & cache-seeding

Hi Jasmine — thanks for looping us in. A few clarifications from our side to help with sizing: 

- POC traffic profile: avg ~1,200 sessions/day, expected ramp to ~400 concurrent sessions during peak test windows.
- Tokens/day expected: ~80k tokens/day in POC.
- Prefixes: the attached CSV is our top 12 prefixes (patient-facing prompts & a few clinician templates). There is PHI in the full histories; we can provide scrubbed versions for seeding.
- Model: we plan to use redwood/med-small-1.0 (FP16) for POC. No 4-bit quantization for this POC.

We are flexible on exclusive GPU residency if that's a blocker; our main ask is that the 85p latency for our flows be demonstrably below 80ms during Apr 5–12. If you can provide an operational playbook for starting the warmup (e.g., give us S3 path to upload scrubbed prefixes and a small runner) that would be fine as well.

We are hoping for a firm yes/no on timeline by Apr 1 to coordinate our internal clinical test window. Happy to join a design/ops call.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Product Ops, Pelican Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 13:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pelican POC: request for onboarding warmup residency & cache-seeding

Appreciate the details — here's a proposed minimal scope that I think balances Pelican's ask with our capacity constraints: 

Minimal POC warmup mode (target implementation):
- A toggle in Dedicated/Private config: "poc_warmup_mode" that reserves a single GPU slot for the target account for up to 72 hours. No permanent changes to scheduling.
- Cache seeding pipeline: simple secure S3 ingest where customer uploads scrubbed prefixes; a background worker replays these prefixes against the pinned instance to populate KV/prefix caches. We will not store PHI in our systems (customer provides scrubbed data).
- Operational knobs: start_time, duration (default 72h), and fallback policy (auto-downgrade to shared pool at expiry).

Estimated cross-team effort: 
- Eng (runtime + orchestrator): 2–3 weeks (Dev + 1 engineer)
- CS/Ops runbook and support: ~2 days to onboard and run initial seed
- Security review/informal signoff: 2–3 days (assuming scrubbed data)

Risks/notes:
- If customer cannot scrub PHI, we need a compliant replay path (longer timeline).
- Capacity: exclusive residency uses 1 GPU slot; if we have overlaps on the dates we may need to prioritize — ops/partner desk will coordinate.

Given the ask that Pelican wants warmup started Apr 4, we can target basic implementation if Eng can start tomorrow and we accept a small operational manual step (CS runs the seed job). That would be a best-effort timeline (Apr 4–6) to enable warmup, with a follow-up to harden automation in the following sprint.

If everyone agrees, I'll draft a scoped ticket and proposed acceptance criteria. Dev — can you confirm if 2–3 weeks estimate still stands and whether you can break out a minimal MVB (manual runbook + toggle) vs fully automated option?

-Marissa
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Pelican POC: request for onboarding warmup residency & cache-seeding

Thanks everyone — sounds like we're converging. Quick next steps: 
- Dev/Marissa: please create the scoped ticket (MVB: manual seed + toggle) and drop an acceptance criteria checklist in the ticket today.
- CS (Grace): I'll coordinate with Pelican to get scrubbed prefixes uploaded to the Drive S3 path Marissa linked.
- Ops (Ben/Karthik): confirm GPU slot availability Apr 4–6 and label the slot for PEL-4921 if approved.
- I'll schedule a 30m design sync tomorrow (Fri) to confirm runbook and who will run the seed. Alex — can you confirm availability 10:00am PT?

Appreciate the quick turn here — this POC is high priority for closing the deal.

Jasmine
